_readme: The declarative list of repositories that consume this hub, and the classes of
hub entry point the inventory grades. linux/scripts/verify_consumer_inventory.py
reads this file; .github/workflows/consumer-inventory.yml runs it on a schedule.
Rationale, the report format and the rules for editing this file:

consumers.name: ANTfrastructure
consumers.note: The hub itself. Present so an entry point reached ONLY from here is visible as such: hub-internal use is not a consumer, and that distinction is the whole point of the report.

consumers.name: BeschleunigerBallett
consumers.note: C++/CMake. Submodule at third_party/ANTfrastructure; uses the four container composite actions and run-lint-gates.sh.

consumers.name: OmniAccelerANT
consumers.note: Flutter/Dart. Submodule at third_party/ANTfrastructure.

consumers.name: OrchestrANT
consumers.note: Python. Calls the python-ci-linux.yml / python-ci-windows.yml reusable workflows.

consumers.name: jotrockenmitlocken
consumers.note: Flutter/Dart. Submodule at third_party/ANTfrastructure.

consumers.name: OxidANT
consumers.note: Rust. Submodule at third_party/ANTfrastructure; bootstraps through scripts/linux/lib/antfrastructure.sh. Its Linux lane calls the 02-toolchain/rust/cargo_*.sh drivers directly by path; three of them were deleted in 6f5aef72 (2026-09-08) as unreached because this repo was not declared here, and restored on 2026-09-09. Its container scripts (scripts/windows/container/*.ps1) import WindowsContainerLog.Common through Resolve-BuildModule.ps1 from the streamed tree since 20a03fb (2026-10-19), by path from a mounted scratch dir before; the same sweep deleted that module and windows/scripts/rust/New-Archive.ps1, and 2026-09-14 restored both. No family checkout names New-Archive.ps1 any more (checked 2026-09-25).

consumers.name: AccelerANTgine
consumers.note: C++/CMake engine, a submodule of OmniAccelerANT and itself a hub consumer (third_party/ANTfrastructure). Reaches cmake-build, ctest-run, coverage, code-quality, docs-build and 01-core/python_uv via antfrastructure_source; run-lint-gates and renovate-local via antfrastructure_exec; its Windows lane imports WindowsOnnx.Common by NAME through Resolve-BuildModule (deleted in 6f5aef72, restored 2026-09-14).

consumers.name: ANThology
consumers.note: Shared Dart package, consumed by OmniAccelerANT and jotrockenmitlocken. It now pins ANTfrastructure at third_party/ANTfrastructure for local tooling and calls the hub's reusable workflows and composite actions at @develop in CI. Inventory grades both routes.

consumers.name: WebDavClient
consumers.note: Python. Calls the python-ci-linux.yml / python-ci-windows.yml reusable workflows (verified 2026-09-14 against a clone; still under the pre-rename name Kataglyphis-ContainerHub at ExternalLib/, which is its own migration item). kataglyphis_webdavclient is imported by windows/scripts/certificates/download_webdav_files.py and by jotrockenmitlocken's scripts/download_markdown_files.py, so the hub is also a consumer of it.

consumers.name: DocumANTation
consumers.note: The Sphinx brand theme and md2pdf, vendored BY the hub at third_party/DocumANTation. It has no ANTfrastructure submodule and calls no hub action; its pins are written by the hub's docs/scripts/sync_versions.py. Declared on 2026-10-07 because verify_workflow_conventions.py refuses a repository consumers.json does not name, so the family lint could not grade its two workflows.

entry_point_classes.why: A composite action is reached as `<owner>/ANTfrastructure/.github/actions/<name>@<ref>`, so the DIRECTORY is the entry point.
Only a workflow that declares workflow_call is callable from another repository; the rest are this repo's own lanes.
The Python gates. Several take a consumer root and are meant to be run from a consumer checkout.

The top-level shell entry points (preflight, the lint gates, the build drivers). Stage scripts under 01-core/ .. 06-packaging/ are deliberately out of scope, though a consumer CAN reach one directly: OxidANT's Linux lane calls 06-packaging/package_archive.sh (found 2026-09-18), so this class under-reports those trees.
Shared shell libraries are also sourced by basename through dynamically selected module directories.
Shared bootstrap dependencies can be opened by basename beside their library.
Consumer scripts can install a shared root-level bootstrap file by path or basename.
The files Sync-SharedConfig copies into every consumer, plus the syncers themselves.
Templates a consumer copies or sources verbatim.
Pester suites the hub publishes for consumers to run against their own tree.

Per-language Windows drivers a consumer calls by hub PATH from its workflow (OxidANT's Windows lane named New-Archive.ps1 this way; no family checkout does any more, checked 2026-09-25). The windows/scripts/*.ps1 class above is non-recursive, so without this row nothing graded them and the 2026-09-08 sweep deleted one that was live.
The PowerShell modules. A consumer asks for one by NAME (Resolve-BuildModulePath -Name 'WindowsBuild.Common'), never by hub path, so the path alone would report every module dead.
CMake modules. A consumer puts the hub's cmake/ on CMAKE_MODULE_PATH and then writes include(Sanitizers), so the path alone would report every one of them dead.
